statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = n - M, where M = max { |S| : S is a subset of {0,1,...,n-1} such that for every two distinct indices i,j in S, end_i <= start_j or end_j <= start_i }. In words, n - r is the maximum number of given intervals that can be kept so that no two kept intervals overlap in more than a shared endpoint, and r is the minimum number of intervals that must be removed.
preconditions: Let n = len(intervals). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, len(intervals[i]) = 2; and with start_i = intervals[i][0] and end_i = intervals[i][1], assume -50000 <= start_i < end_i <= 50000.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r; in particular, it does not fail, panic, overflow, or access an interval out of bounds.
preconditions: Let n = len(intervals). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, len(intervals[i]) = 2; and with start_i = intervals[i][0] and end_i = intervals[i][1], assume -50000 <= start_i < end_i <= 50000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 0 <= r.
preconditions: Let n = len(intervals). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, len(intervals[i]) = 2; and with start_i = intervals[i][0] and end_i = intervals[i][1], assume -50000 <= start_i < end_i <= 50000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r <= n - 1.
preconditions: Let n = len(intervals). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, len(intervals[i]) = 2; and with start_i = intervals[i][0] and end_i = intervals[i][1], assume -50000 <= start_i < end_i <= 50000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 0 if and only if for every pair of indices i,j with 0 <= i < j < n, end_i <= start_j or end_j <= start_i.
preconditions: Let n = len(intervals). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, len(intervals[i]) = 2; and with start_i = intervals[i][0] and end_i = intervals[i][1], assume -50000 <= start_i < end_i <= 50000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there exists a subset S of {0,1,...,n-1} such that |S| = n - r and for every two distinct indices i,j in S, end_i <= start_j or end_j <= start_i.
preconditions: Let n = len(intervals). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, len(intervals[i]) = 2; and with start_i = intervals[i][0] and end_i = intervals[i][1], assume -50000 <= start_i < end_i <= 50000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every subset S of {0,1,...,n-1} with the property that for all distinct i,j in S, end_i <= start_j or end_j <= start_i, we have |S| <= n - r.
preconditions: Let n = len(intervals). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, len(intervals[i]) = 2; and with start_i = intervals[i][0] and end_i = intervals[i][1], assume -50000 <= start_i < end_i <= 50000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = n - 1 if and only if for every pair of indices i,j with 0 <= i < j < n, neither end_i <= start_j nor end_j <= start_i (equivalently start_i < end_j and start_j < end_i).
preconditions: Let n = len(intervals). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, len(intervals[i]) = 2; and with start_i = intervals[i][0] and end_i = intervals[i][1], assume -50000 <= start_i < end_i <= 50000.

statement: For any two inputs A and B satisfying the preconditions with len(A) = len(B) = n, and any permutation π of {0,1,...,n-1} such that B[i][0] = A[π(i)][0] and B[i][1] = A[π(i)][1] for every i with 0 <= i < n, if r_A is a result returned by the function on A and r_B is a result returned by the function on B, then r_A = r_B.
preconditions: Both A and B are interval lists satisfying the input conditions: for X in {A,B}, letting n_X = len(X), we have 1 <= n_X <= 100000, len(X[i]) = 2 for every 0 <= i < n_X, and -50000 <= X[i][0] < X[i][1] <= 50000 for every 0 <= i < n_X.

statement: For any two inputs A and B satisfying the preconditions with len(A) = len(B) = n and any integer c such that for every i with 0 <= i < n, B[i][0] = A[i][0] + c and B[i][1] = A[i][1] + c, if r_A is a result returned by the function on A and r_B is a result returned by the function on B, then r_A = r_B.
preconditions: Both A and B are interval lists satisfying the input conditions: for X in {A,B}, letting n_X = len(X), we have 1 <= n_X <= 100000, len(X[i]) = 2 for every 0 <= i < n_X, and -50000 <= X[i][0] < X[i][1] <= 50000 for every 0 <= i < n_X.

statement: For any two inputs A and B satisfying the preconditions with len(A) = len(B) = n and for every i with 0 <= i < n, B[i][0] = -A[i][1] and B[i][1] = -A[i][0], if r_A is a result returned by the function on A and r_B is a result returned by the function on B, then r_A = r_B.
preconditions: Both A and B are interval lists satisfying the input conditions: for X in {A,B}, letting n_X = len(X), we have 1 <= n_X <= 100000, len(X[i]) = 2 for every 0 <= i < n_X, and -50000 <= X[i][0] < X[i][1] <= 50000 for every 0 <= i < n_X.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 1 if and only if there exists an index k with 0 <= k < n such that (i) for every two distinct indices i,j in {0,1,...,n-1} \ {k}, end_i <= start_j or end_j <= start_i, and (ii) the whole set {0,1,...,n-1} is not pairwise non-overlapping, meaning there exist i,j with 0 <= i < j < n such that neither end_i <= start_j nor end_j <= start_i.
preconditions: Let n = len(intervals). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, len(intervals[i]) = 2; and with start_i = intervals[i][0] and end_i = intervals[i][1], assume -50000 <= start_i < end_i <= 50000.

statement: Let n = len(A). Assume len(B) = n + 1, B[i] = A[i] for every 0 <= i < n, and the last interval B[n] is non-overlapping with every A[i], i.e. for every i with 0 <= i < n, A[i][1] <= B[n][0] or B[n][1] <= A[i][0]. If r_A is a result returned by the function on A and r_B is a result returned by the function on B, then r_A = r_B.
preconditions: Both A and B are interval lists satisfying the input conditions: for X in {A,B}, letting n_X = len(X), we have 1 <= n_X <= 100000, len(X[i]) = 2 for every 0 <= i < n_X, and -50000 <= X[i][0] < X[i][1] <= 50000 for every 0 <= i < n_X.

statement: If r_A is a result returned by the function on A and r_B is a result returned by the function on B, then r_A <= r_B <= r_A + 1. In words, adding one interval can never decrease the minimum number of removals and can increase it by at most one.
preconditions: Both A and B are interval lists satisfying the input conditions: for X in {A,B}, letting n_X = len(X), we have 1 <= n_X <= 100000, len(X[i]) = 2 for every 0 <= i < n_X, and -50000 <= X[i][0] < X[i][1] <= 50000 for every 0 <= i < n_X. Let n = len(A). Assume len(B) = n + 1, B[i] = A[i] for every 0 <= i < n, and B[n] is any interval satisfying len(B[n]) = 2 and -50000 <= B[n][0] < B[n][1] <= 50000 (i.e. B is A with one extra interval appended).
